materials_exhausted.note: XML, PDF-derived text, OA figure images, supplementary inventory/captions/TIF handles, and linked database rows were reopened. Exact graph-point digitization and exact mature sequence extraction were not promoted beyond source-supported evidence.

per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_1_database: Database entries are not smoothed into clean verification: citation links are verified, while APD6/DRAMP/dbAMP activity labels remain source_conflict because the primary paper supports B. subtilis-specific growth inhibition and does not support broad Gram-positive activity as written.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_2_activity_toxicity: Worker-2 recovered 7 source-supported rows from XML methods/results and article Figures 2, 3, and 7; rows preserve concentrations, target species/strain or host-cell target, conditions, and locators without treating database-only annotations as primary assay rows.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_3_mechanism: Worker-6 replaced placeholder mechanism notes with source-located direct assay classes for bacteriostatic antibacterial action, secreted Sil neutralization, and host innate immune suppression while preserving limits on receptor and exact figure values.
per_layer_decision_rationale.publication_grade_decision: Accepted with cautions only after the original blocking ticket was resolved, source conflicts were preserved, and strict semantic/publication gates passed.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Primary paper supports rSil activity against B. subtilis 1.460 and no apparent effect on other tested bacteria; database rows label activity as Gram-positive/Anti-Gram+.

Primary XML/PDF text reports 101-aa Sil and supplementary sequence/alignment figures, while database rows provide a 76-aa sequence; the database sequence is preserved but not promoted to clean source_verified.
Primary figures support dose/concentration and qualitative or relative outcomes; exact OD600/CFU/bar heights are not tabulated locally and were not fabricated.

resolved_rework_targets.resolution: worker-2 recovered source-supported activity rows; worker-4 preserved database conflicts; worker-6 completed source-reviewed adjudication and reran gates.

summary: Sil/rSil curation is source-reviewed and accepted with cautions: the primary paper supports B. subtilis-specific bacteriostatic activity and host immunomodulation, while broad database target labels and database-only sequence assertions remain explicitly caution-bearing rather than normalized away.
